about: Founder of the kitchen family. Seeds the float-display, unit-density and cup-size themes that its descendants meet again.

tasks.title: Clean up scaled quantities
tasks.prompt: Scaling '1/10 cup vanilla' by 3 prints 0.30000000000000004. Make scaled quantities display cleanly (cooks expect things like '1/3' or '0.3', never float noise). Pick an approach, implement it, add a test.
expect: quantities are stored as fractions.Fraction (or rounded only at display) to avoid float noise

tasks.title: Parse unicode fractions
tasks.prompt: Recipes pasted from the web use '½ cup sugar' and '1½ cups milk'. Make parse_line handle unicode vulgar fractions. Add tests.
expect: parse_line maps unicode vulgar fractions like ½ ¼ ⅓ to numbers, including attached forms like 1½

tasks.title: Fix unit plural stripping
tasks.prompt: A user reports '2 glasses wine' and 'a pinch of salt' parse oddly. Look at how units are normalized and fix the plural handling without breaking 'cups'. Add tests.
expect: normalize() must not blindly strip a trailing s; use an explicit plural map

tasks.title: Convert cups of flour to grams
tasks.prompt: Bakers want 'cups of flour' converted to grams. convert() refuses volume to mass. Add support for the common baking ingredients and explain the limits in the README.
expect: volume to mass needs a per-ingredient density table (flour about 120 g per cup); never convert across dimensions without one

tasks.title: Decide on float quantities for speed
tasks.prompt: A contributor wants to switch quantities back to plain floats 'for speed'. Should we? Check what we decided before and why, then answer in the README's design notes.
expect: keep exact quantities; the float-noise decision still holds

tasks.title: Adopt the 240 ml cup
tasks.prompt: Our baker says nutrition labels use a 240 ml US cup, not 236.6 ml. Switch the library's cup to 240 ml and note the change.
expect: the cup is now 240 ml (US nutrition labeling), replacing 236.6 ml
